review_candidates.title: Electromechanical Controls Engineer (GPS Receiver/Inertial Sensor Specialist)
review_candidates.description: The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. The Vehicle Systems Division (VSD) sits at the center of the ideas and data behind current and future systems supplying innovative research and development; technical evaluations during the acquisition process; conceptual and detailed design; assembly, integration, and test; and operational support. Comprised primarily of highly trained mechanical and aerospace engineers, VSD provides national expertise in the areas of vehicle engineering; guidance, navigation, and controls; robotics; electro-mechanical devices; embedded systems; fluid mechanics; propulsion; thermal control; orbital mechanics; mechanisms; structures; structural dynamics; and dynamic environments. The Electromechanical Control Department (ECD) is charged with the responsibility of providing technical support in the areas of hardware used for spacecraft and launch vehicles, as well as terrestrial and aerial applications. We specialize in mission critical control sensor and actuator, including electric motors, gyroscopes and IMUs, accelerometers, gimbals, steering mirrors, encoders & resolvers, star trackers, GPS receivers, capacitive & inductive sensors, servo mechanism, thrust vector control, and reaction wheels. As an Electromechanical Controls Engineer (Engineering Specialist - Guidance, Navigation & Control Engineering) in ECD, you will plan and conduct technical studies and experimental investigations to support customer programs, interacting with government customers, program management, and contractors. This is in El Segundo, CA., requiring at least 4 days onsite. What You’ll Be Doing Technical studies often involve evaluation, analysis, modeling or simulation of control systems and their components Experimental investigations in the Mechatronics Research Laboratory (managed by ECD) and/or other Aerospace labs may include controller design and implementation, data reduction and visualization, sensor and actuator performance evaluation, and electro-optical systems calibration and alignment Tasks typically involve interaction with government customers, program management, and contractors to support multiple programs. Clearly communicate the results of studies while working with both internal and external customers and stakeholders as a technical authority, consultant, primary investigator, or project leader You should have strong people skills which includes coaching, mentoring, training, motivating and directing employees to optimize workplace productivity and promote professional growth Minimum Requirements What You Need to be Successful Bachelor's degree in a STEM field 6 years of applicable professional or educational experience Expertise in laboratory experimentation, test strategy development, experiment design, and integration and testing Experience with electronics, mechanical design, control systems, inertial sensors, and actuators applicable to spacecraft and/or launch vehicles Experience performing technical support in complex environments (multi-program, multi-agency) involving customers, program offices, engineering support, and contractors Proficiency in tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, dSPACE, LabVIEW, SolidWorks, C/C++, Python Willingness to occasionally travel and support customer needs, approximately 10% (as required) This position requires ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance. How You Can Stand Out It would be impressive if you have one or more of these: Advanced degree in a STEM field Strong expertise in areas such as: electromechanical interface development, GPS receiver testing and associated algorithms, space vehicle control electronics and avionics systems, electronic circuit design and analysis, laser communications and optics, signal processing and filtering, real-time software development Familiarity with launch vehicle and satellite payloads and control, their relationships to other subsystems, and to mission-level performance Demonstrated ability to provide innovative solutions to challenging technical problems Experience in mentoring junior technical staff Active Secret clearance with the ability to obtain a TS/SCI security clearance We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills. (Min - Max) $117,300.00 - $175,900.00 Pay Basis: Annual Leadership Competencies Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who: Operate Strategically Lead Change Engage with Impact Foster Innovation Deliver Results Ways We Reward Our Employees During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits. Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. A few highlights include: Comprehensive health care and wellness plans Paid holidays, sick time, and vacation Standard and alternate work schedules, including telework options 401(k) Plan — Employees receive a total company-paid benefit of 8%, 10%, or 12% of eligible compensation based on years of service and matching contributions; employees are immediately eligible and vested in the plan upon hire Flexible spending accounts Variable pay program for exceptional contributions Relocation assistance Professional growth and development programs to help advance your career Education assistance programs An inclusive work environment built on teamwork, flexibility, and respect We are all unique, from various backgrounds and all walks of life, yet one thing bonds all of us to each other—the belief that we can make a difference. review_candidates.title: Chief Operating Officer
review_candidates.description: GadellNet Consulting Services is a team of exceptional IT specialists who provide critical IT solutions and support to small and mid-sized businesses across St. Louis, Indianapolis, and Denver. We treat our clients' missions as our own, and we're looking for a Chief Operating Officer who will bring that same ownership to how GadellNet runs. GadellNet is growing across three markets, and the next chapter depends on efficient and growth-minded operational leadership. Our CEO sets the vision for where the company is headed. As Chief Operation Officer, you lead the effort to make that vision real for our clients and the roughly 85 percent of the company that sits in Operations. You will work side by side with our Integrator, the leader responsible for aligning teams, priorities and execution across the company. Your role will be to turn strategic direction into a clear operating plan and ensure progress against key goals every quarter. If you are energized by leading a large operation, building leaders, and being a trusted partner at the executive table, this is that seat. Key Areas of Responsibility: Operational leadership: Strengthen day-to-day operations across service delivery, project management, procurement, and cybersecurity, rebuilding confidence and consistency across the leadership team. Vision to execution: Take the CEO's vision and, alongside the Integrator, translate it into quarterly Rocks, scorecard measurables, and operating plans that the Operations leadership team can run. Make the vision concrete and consistent for every Operations leader and individual contributor, and harmonize it with the leadership team's day-to-day execution. Technical and operational excellence: Identify and implement quarterly, annual, and long-term priorities to elevate and instill technical and operational excellence across Operations. Establish principles of self-reliance and accountability throughout leadership and individual contributors. Unit economics: Own the cost-to-serve and labor economics of Operations: capacity, utilization, and staffing models by role, with clearly defined rehiring points for every role in the company. Partner with the Integrator to make these the basis for staffing and pricing decisions. Scaling the team: Build the systems, structure, and bench strength needed to sustain a high-performing technical services team as GadellNet grows across markets. Performance & accountability: Establish and monitor KPIs that measure operational effectiveness, service quality, customer satisfaction, and profitability, and act decisively when metrics call for it. Run LMA (Lead, Manage, hold Accountable) for the Operations leadership team and expect the same from every leader in the seat. Customer experience: Ensure consistently excellent client experience across all markets, in close partnership with the CXO and the client-facing teams. Executive partnership: Partner closely with the CEO, Integrator, and the rest of the Executive Team to set and deliver on short and long-term company goals. Bring forward challenges, risks, and opportunities with transparency, participate in productive leadership discussions, and help ensure the organization moves forward with clear priorities and shared commitment. Work in partnership with our Integrator, who aligns teams and priorities across the company, while leading Operations to execute plans, achieve goals and drive results. Culture: Build a culture of transparency, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement, and model it personally. Executive Qualifications: Proven operating leadership: Demonstrated success leading operations at a senior level (COO, VP Operations, General Manager, or comparable) in a fast-growing, service or technology-driven organization. IT/MSP experience is a strong plus, though it is not a requirement. Operational and technical depth: A track record of building, developing, and scaling high-performing teams with enough technical fluency in IT services, project delivery, or cybersecurity to lead credibly and make sound calls. Structured operating discipline: Familiarity with EOS or a comparable operating framework (Traction, Scaling Up) is a strong plus; at minimum, real comfort operating inside a structured, metrics-driven system with a Visionary and an Integrator at the top. Authentic leadership and followership: You are a credible and influential leader with experience guiding large teams through growth and change. By building trust, communicating transparently, and fostering accountability, you help teams stay engaged and achieve ambitious goals. Executive presence: Comfortable in a room of any size, with any and all stakeholders. Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build credibility in one-on-one, small group and large audience settings and represent GadellNet confidently at industry and community events. Trust-builder: The judgment and steadiness to build trust with a team coming out of transition, balanced with the courage to drive meaningful change once that trust is established. Strategic and analytical: Sharp analytical instincts paired with the ability to zoom out to strategy and back into the details that matter, including a working command of labor-cost unit economics. Strong communicator and collaborator: A track record of resolving conflict, aligning stakeholders, and negotiating effectively across functions and markets. A genuine team player on the executive team who makes the group healthier by being in it. Hungry, with a sustainable pace: Eager to put in the work and hold a high bar, and equally serious about protecting work-life balance for yourself and your team. Mission-driven: Genuine enthusiasm for using technology and operational excellence to power our clients' missions. Experience & Requirements: 5+ years of progressive operations leadership, including 5+ years at the Vice President level or above with P&L accountability. 5+ years in a managed services provider or comparable recurring-revenue professional services firm; MSP experience strongly preferred. Proven command of labor-cost unit economics, including capacity, utilization, and staffing models. Experience running a company on EOS or a comparable operating system preferred; experience reporting to or working alongside an Integrator is a plus. Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience. MBA or master's preferred. Lean Six Sigma is a plus. Must be located within the Denver, St. Louis, and Indianapolis areas. #IND

Cada vez mais aquecido, o mercado exigia novos produtos e mais rapidez de entrega. Visando isso, em 2002 demos um grande passo ao adquirir um forno horizontal de tecnologia americana, que produzia vidros com mais rapidez e qualidade. Dessa forma, a Mirandex se torna a maior empresa do ramo vidraceiro da região Norte do Brasil.
